findings.title: Divine allocation and human claims
findings.claim: A question about human claims of selection is bracketed by the Lord's knowledge and actual differentiated prophetic favor. Within that frame, the focus places mercy and punishment under the Lord's will and denies the messenger delegated custody, making outcome and rank legible as divine allocation rather than human entitlement.
findings.mechanism: The initial reading contrasts divine knowledge with ordinary ignorance. Before the focus, 17:40 questions a claimed selection; after it, 17:55 repeats the Lord-knows-best formula and says some prophets were favored over others. The focus between them places mercy and punishment under the Lord's will and denies the messenger as wakil. This sequence shifts attention from knowledge in general to who may claim or administer differentiated outcomes, without making prophetic gifts identical to the addressees' mercy or punishment.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus is heard within both a question of humanly asserted selection and a statement of divine differentiation: the messenger's role in the distribution is bounded even as distinct forms of favor remain in view.

The connection evidence for 17:40 describes sovereignty and mercy but says that ayah does not make a specific allocation claim. The bracket makes an entitlement reading possible without equating the allocations or establishing a universal social rule.

findings.title: Warning within divine governance
findings.claim: The immediate context gives a positive shape to the denied wakil role: outcomes are written and governed, signs are sent as warning, and people are tested, while the messenger's sending remains transmission rather than control of the recipients' response.
findings.mechanism: The initial reading treats not being a custodian as a negative limitation alone. 17:58 places outcomes in a written register; 17:59 says signs are sent as warning; 17:60 joins the Lord's encompassing of people to a vision and tree that test them and to further transgression. The focus's sending and wakil clauses contact this distribution of agency, changing the negative limit into a bounded role: the messenger conveys and warns within divine governance.
findings.reader_payoff: Non-custody becomes a place within an active arrangement of agency: what is sent can warn and expose, while the Lord governs outcomes and the response is not enforced.
findings.containment: The force of 17:60's encompassing may be knowledge, securing, or threatened defeat; warning and trial do not guarantee reception. This contextual reading does not settle that image or imply that every sign has the same effect.

findings.title: Will and the field of things
findings.claim: As an exploratory lexical resonance, the focus's repeated will verbs may be heard beside the pericope's 'thing' that praises God: the Lord's willing is heard as bringing mercy or punishment into the field of what exists, while human understanding remains limited.
